auditMethod: Official city/state source review; facts with incomplete machine-readable support are explicitly flagged for follow-up.

cities.name: Chandler
cities.max: Up to 5 chickens
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Building permit if coop exceeds 120 sq ft or has utilities
cities.placement: Rear/side yards; coop at least 5 ft from every property line
cities.note: Rear-yard placement still needs manual confirmation.

audit.note: Official Chandler backyard chicken ordinance confirms up to 5 chickens, no roosters, rear/side-yard confinement, 5-ft property-line coop setback, and permit triggers for larger/utility-served coops.

cities.name: Mesa
cities.max: 10 fowl/rabbits total on lots under ½ acre
cities.roosters: Allowed only if they do not create a noise disturbance
cities.permit: Check parcel-specific zoning/building requirements
cities.placement: Fowl must be contained; city code has enclosure-distance rules
cities.note: Automatic geometry is disabled until Mesa's code-specific distance rule is modeled.

audit.note: Official Mesa guidance confirms 10 fowl/rabbits total on lots under 1/2 acre, rooster noise restriction, and code-specific containment distance rules.

cities.name: Phoenix
cities.max: Up to 6 poultry on the first ½ acre; larger lots scale under the ordinance, and written adjoining-neighbor consent can allow more on lots ½ acre or less
cities.roosters: Male poultry are allowed only if incapable of making vocal noise that disturbs nearby residents
cities.permit: Verify zoning and accessory-structure requirements for the property
cities.placement: Rear or side yard; enclosure at least 20 ft from a neighboring property line unless adjoining owners/occupants consent in writing; no front-yard poultry
cities.note: Phoenix uses a 20-ft neighboring-property-line rule plus rear/side-yard placement, with written-consent exceptions. The planner cannot yet identify which drawn boundary is a neighboring property line or determine legal yard orientation.

audit.note: Re-verified after the 2024 Phoenix poultry amendment. Current baseline is 6 poultry on the first 1/2 acre with written-consent/larger-lot provisions and a 20-ft neighboring-property-line enclosure rule.

cities.name: Tempe
cities.max: Up to 6 domestic chickens per lot
cities.roosters: Prohibited except in the AG district
cities.permit: A use permit may be available to exceed the standard quantity
cities.placement: On lots under 1 acre, chicken enclosures may not exceed the fence/wall height
cities.note: The cited city page does not provide one universal chicken-enclosure property-line setback.

audit.note: Official Tempe code guidance confirms up to 6 domestic chickens, roosters prohibited except AG zoning, use-permit path for higher quantities, and enclosure-height rule on lots under 1 acre.

cities.name: San Diego
cities.max: 5, 15, or 25 depending on separation
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Check building/zoning rules for the structure
cities.placement: Typical 5-hen case: rear yard, 5 ft side and 13 ft rear setbacks
cities.note: Typical single-family guidance only; exact zoning setbacks can differ.

audit.note: Official San Diego guidance and Municipal Code confirm the 5/15/25 chicken tiers and no-rooster rule; the common 5-hen case uses rear-yard placement with 5-ft side and 13-ft rear setbacks.

cities.name: Sacramento
cities.max: Up to 3 chickens per residential parcel
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Annual chicken license and chicken coop permit required
cities.placement: Rear yard only; coop at least 20 ft from the nearest neighboring dwelling
cities.note: The key distance is to a neighboring dwelling, so parcel geometry alone is not enough.

audit.note: Official Sacramento poultry licensing page confirms maximum 3 chickens, no roosters, annual chicken licenses and coop permit, rear-yard placement, and 20-ft separation from nearest neighboring dwelling.

cities.name: Denver
cities.max: Up to 8 hens/ducks combined
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Food-Producing Animals permit: one-time $25 per property
cities.placement: Rear 50% of lot; housing structures 15 ft from certain neighboring dwellings
cities.note: The planner cannot yet verify neighboring dwelling distances.

audit.note: Official Denver animal guidance confirms an FPA permit and up to 8 hens/ducks combined; zoning code confirms rear 50% placement and 15-ft separation from specified neighboring dwellings.

cities.name: Colorado Springs
cities.max: Up to 10 rabbits or chickens aged 6 months or older
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Coops must comply with applicable zoning/building rules for accessory structures
cities.placement: At least 4 sq ft of shelter space per chicken; accessory-structure setbacks vary by zoning/size
cities.note: There is no single universal coop setback in the cited city guidance; accessory-structure rules vary.

audit.note: Official Colorado Springs guidance confirms up to 10 rabbits/chickens aged 6 months or older, roosters prohibited, 4 sq ft shelter per bird, and accessory-structure code requirements.

cities.name: Portland
cities.max: 4 on any lot; 6 on lots ≥10,000 sq ft
cities.roosters: Generally prohibited outside qualifying agricultural use
cities.permit: No livestock permit for standard backyard chickens
cities.placement: Structures 3 ft from side/rear lines and 10 ft from front line
cities.note: Direct property-line setbacks are supported by the planner.

audit.note: Official Portland code, amended effective January 10, 2025, confirms 4 small fowl on any lot, 6 on lots >=10,000 sq ft, rooster restrictions, no standard livestock permit, and current facility standards.

cities.name: Eugene
cities.max: On lots under 20,000 sq ft: up to 6 adult + 6 under 6 months
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: No license; building permit generally not required for enclosure ≤200 sq ft and ≤10 ft high
cities.placement: Animal shelters and covered runs at least 10 ft from all property lines unless adjacent owner authorizes closer placement
cities.note: The 10-ft property-line rule is directly supported; parcel zoning and CC&Rs still need verification.

audit.note: Official Eugene Urban Animal Keeping guidance confirms up to 6 adult and 6 under-6-month chickens/domestic fowl on lots under 20,000 sq ft, no roosters, 10-ft shelter/run setback from property lines unless written adjacent-owner authorization, and the <=200 sq ft / <=10 ft enclosure permit threshold.

cities.name: Salem
cities.max: Up to 12 poultry total per property
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: No permit or license required for standard poultry keeping
cities.placement: Rear yard; 3 ft from other buildings on site and 25 ft from a residence on adjacent property
cities.note: The key rule measures to neighboring residences, not simply the property line.

audit.note: Official Salem poultry guidance confirms maximum 12 poultry, no roosters, no standard permit/license, rear-yard facility placement, 3-ft on-site building separation, and 25-ft separation from an adjacent residence.

cities.name: Gresham
cities.max: Up to 3 adult hens on eligible single-family property
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Chicken permit required; city lists a $50 two-year permit
cities.placement: Rear yard; coop/run 10 ft from property lines; coop 25 ft from neighboring dwelling
cities.note: The city has both a property-line rule and a neighboring-dwelling rule, so full automation needs neighbor-building data.

audit.note: Official Gresham guidance confirms permit requirement, up to 3 adult hens, no roosters, rear-yard placement, 10-ft property-line separation, and 25-ft neighboring-dwelling separation.

cities.name: Seattle
cities.max: Up to 8 domestic fowl on a standard lot
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: No general chicken permit stated on the city overview
cities.placement: Chicken structures at least 10 ft from residential structures on adjacent lots
cities.note: Accurate automation needs neighboring building footprints.

audit.note: Official Seattle animal guidance and SDCI Tip 244 confirm up to 8 domestic fowl on a standard lot, no roosters, and a 10-ft separation between fowl structures and residential structures on adjacent lots.

cities.name: Spokane
cities.max: 1 chicken/fowl per 1,000 sq ft of lot area
cities.roosters: Only allowed in RA zone
cities.permit: Chickens are excluded from the WSU animal-keeping certification requirement
cities.placement: Animal enclosures follow residential accessory-structure setbacks
cities.note: Accessory-structure setbacks depend on the property's zoning and cannot be represented by one citywide number.

audit.note: Official Spokane Municipal Code confirms one small domestic animal/fowl per 1,000 sq ft of lot area and zoning-based animal-keeping standards; rooster allowance remains limited by zoning.

cities.name: Vancouver
cities.max: Chickens are allowed; verify parcel-specific quantity/animal standards
cities.roosters: Prohibited
cities.permit: Check zoning and accessory-structure requirements for the property
cities.placement: Domestic-animal and accessory-structure rules apply
cities.note: The city's public FAQ confirms chickens are allowed and roosters are not, but does not state one universal coop setback.

audit.note: Official Vancouver guidance confirms chickens are allowed and roosters/peacocks are prohibited. It does not publish one universal quantity or coop setback on the cited page, so CoopCheck correctly keeps parcel-specific details manual.

cities.name: Austin
cities.max: Chickens allowed in most residential areas; quantity limits depend on code
cities.roosters: Check current city animal/noise rules
cities.permit: Verify enclosure/building requirements for the property
cities.placement: For 2+ chickens, enclosures should be at least 30 ft from adjacent residences or businesses
cities.note: Austin's cited rule measures from adjacent residences/businesses rather than the property line.

audit.note: Official Austin guidance confirms chickens are allowed in most residential areas and enclosures for 2+ chickens should be at least 30 ft from adjacent residences/businesses. Quantity limits remain code/parcel dependent.

cities.name: Arlington
cities.max: Up to 4 chickens without distance or lot-size restrictions; larger flocks have extra rules
cities.roosters: Prohibited except agricultural zoning
cities.permit: Check accessory-structure permit rules for the coop itself
cities.placement: For 5+ chickens, city rules add 50-ft dwelling-distance and lot-size thresholds
cities.note: The rule changes with flock size and measures from nearby dwellings.

audit.note: Official Arlington guidance confirms up to 4 chickens without distance/lot-size restrictions; larger flocks trigger 50-ft dwelling-distance and lot-size thresholds; roosters are prohibited except agricultural zoning.

cities.name: Fort Worth
cities.max: Up to 12 fowl on lots ½ acre or less; higher limits on larger lots
cities.roosters: Up to 2 roosters within the stated fowl limits
cities.permit: Check zoning/building requirements for coop structures
cities.placement: Pens/coops must be more than 50 ft from regulated structures
cities.note: The 50-ft rule is measured from regulated structures, not simply property lines.

audit.note: Official Fort Worth guidance confirms 12 fowl on lots 1/2 acre or less, up to 2 roosters within limits, larger-lot tiers, and >50-ft separation from regulated structures.
